decisions: Direction: design doc §5 hybrid — local ghoztty-agent owns PTYs; viewer keeps a layout+sessionId manifest; agent later gains disk metadata for reboot floor. User approved 2026-07-13 ('let's try it').
v0 local transport = loopback TCP (both ends already exist: agent --listen, ghostty_remote_connection_new_tcp). Unix-socket + peercred is a hardening task AFTER the headline E2E works (T09).
session-persistence is an opt-in config flag initially (default off) so the debug app stays usable throughout.
Ring stays 2 MB default for the demo; configurable size + 16 MB default comes with T11.
Reboot recovery (agent disk persistence, RELAUNCH) comes after the upgrade demo (T12/T13) — the upgrade scenario keeps the agent alive, so it does not need disk persistence.

Future direction (user, 2026-07-16): cross-machine session RESUME. Scenario: a bunch of windows are live on machine X (reachable via relay); the user physically moves to machine Y, hits Cmd-Shift-N, sees X in the machine list, expands to see X's ACTIVE sessions, and resumes one or ALL of them 'on the local machine'. Clarified semantics: the PTYs KEEP RUNNING on X's agent (a running process can't migrate hosts) — 'resume on local machine' means local VIEWER windows on Y ATTACH to the live remote sessions on X over the relay, i.e. the SAME remote-attach mechanism as the local-persistence restore (presentRemoteWindow(sessionID:) / the relay ATTACH path), just driven from a session BROWSER instead of a saved manifest. Needs: (a) enumerate a machine's live sessions [T10 agent LIST_SESSIONS + a viewer-side RPC that can target ANY machine connection, not only the local agent], (b) chooser UI to browse + pick sessions [T16], (c) single-session attach from the browser [T17], (d) for 'resume ALL', the window/tab/split TOPOLOGY must be reachable from Y — today T05/T06 store the layout manifest ONLY in the owning viewer's local Application Support, so the agent (or account) has to own a layout blob [T18]. OPEN design Q: layout lives on the AGENT (Option A — fits the existing architecture; the agent already owns sessions + gains disk metadata in T12; the local viewer manifest becomes a cache/projection) vs SYNCED via the account/relay (Option B — needs account storage, works even when X's agent is offline). Leaning Option A. Tasks T16–T18.

For zsh/fish/elvish it returns null (their integration is env-only; forwarding argv would STRIP the `-li` login/interactive flags — the agent default is exactly right for them). For bash/nushell it splits integration.command via argIterator (ArgIteratorGeneral does the shell word-split + quote-processing nushell's `--execute 'use ghostty *'` single-token needs), dupes each arg into `alloc`, returns the array (caller frees at block exit after Remote.init dupes). Caller (Surface.init remote branch) forwards the returned argv via OPEN.argv ONLY when remote_command==null — the rewrite is the full interactive-shell invocation and must not coexist with a user command (would run the shell instead of the command); a command-pane keeps `-lic <cmd>` (bash/nushell integration for a command-running pane is out of scope). tasks.notes: 2026-07-15: done. ROOT CAUSE of the destruction: the restore liveness probe inferred 'session alive' from GET_CWD returning a non-empty cwd. During a fast relaunch the agent still had the dead app's bridge bound, so the child cwd read failed → empty reply → EVERY session read as dead → all entries removed, though the sessions were alive in the agent's table. FIX (three layers): (1) Protocol: CWD reply gains additive `found: ?bool` — the agent sets it from `getByIdStr(session_id) != null`, i.e. TABLE PRESENCE, which is independent of whether the child/bridge cwd read succeeds. This is the real cure: existence is now answered from the store, not inferred from cwd. Older agents omit the field. (2) Client: new Connection.probeSessionTimeout → tri-state {alive,dead,unknown}: ok=true OR found=true ⇒ alive; found=false ⇒ POSITIVE dead; timeout/malformed/old-agent(found=nil) ⇒ unknown. Exported as ghostty_remote_connection_probe_session (c_int 1/0/-1) in embedded.zig + ghostty.h. (3) Swift drop policy (SessionLayoutRestore): probeSessions now returns [sessionID: .alive/.dead/.unknown]; an entry is forgotten ONLY when EVERY leaf is POSITIVELY .dead — .unknown or missing-id leaves keep the entry AND rebuild+attach it (a live session re-attaches; a truly-gone one shows its exited overlay but the layout survives to retry next launch). BONUS crash-safety: SurfaceView now stashes expectedRemoteSessionID from its creation config, and manifest sync falls back to it when the live id is unavailable (e.g. ghostty_surface_new failed) so a failed-restore sync can't blank a recorded id. Also added an @errorReturnTrace() dump on the ghostty_surface_new failure path (the 'poisoned connection' OutOfMemory) so a recurrence attributes the failing `try` — see below. COMMIT: cda38f18f. tasks.notes: 2026-07-15: done. ROOT CAUSE was NOT agent-side (the ATTACH gap-fill at server.zig:784-816 was correct) — it was a CLIENT-side registration RACE. The client uses TWO separate reader threads over TWO independent streams (connection.zig: control_thread + data_thread, `control`/`data` Streams). On ATTACH the agent frames ATTACHED on the CONTROL lane and the whole ring replay as DATA on the DATA lane. The client only calls channels.register(ch) AFTER the control-lane ATTACHED reply unblocks the caller (connection.zig:1597, attachChannelCancellable). Because the two lanes have NO cross-stream ordering, the data thread frequently ran routeInboundData for the replay DATA BEFORE register() completed → ChannelTable.pushTo found no channel → returned .unknown → bytes DROPPED (inbound_ring.zig old line 388). Microsecond race → per-pane coin-flip, exactly the 'same agent, same cycle, different panes' symptom. Fresh OPEN-new rarely bit because a new shell emits no output for ~ms; ATTACH replay dumps the ring instantly. FIX (client-only, additive): ChannelTable gained a bounded pre-registration buffer `pending: map<channel, ArrayList(u8)>`. pushTo now BUFFERS bytes for a not-yet-registered channel (new RouteResult variant `.buffered`) instead of dropping; register() FLUSHES pending[ch.id] into the ring under the SAME mutex right after map.put, so buffered (pre-register) bytes always precede live (post-register) bytes and none are lost — atomic vs. concurrent pushTo. Bounds: max_pending_bytes_per_channel=256KiB (one client ring), max_pending_channels=16 (hostile-input cap); over-cap excess dropped (old behavior); deregister/deinit free un-claimed buffers. connection.zig routeInboundData treats `.buffered` like `.unknown` (no FLOW). Since real ATTACH always sends last_byte_offset=0 (Remote.zig:264, resync_active=false), no resync-trim interaction; test_client resync path pre-registers so never buffers. This ALSO closes the same latent race for OPEN-new. COMMIT: 4337a9c23. TESTS: inbound_ring standalone 11/11 (3 new: in-order flush T06c, per-channel byte cap, channel-count cap); connection.zig 93/93 (was 90); zig build test-agent exit 0; full app build OK. LIVE E2E (fresh fixture: 2 windows / 4 panes A0/A1/B0/B1, each a unique `echo PANE=n PID=$$; while true tick` loop, agent pid 43438, shells 43441/45205/45448/45688): ran 3x kill -9 + INSTANT (0s) relaunch AND 1x graceful AppleScript quit + relaunch. EVERY cycle, ALL 4 panes replayed pre-gap scrollback (oldest replayed tick well before the pre-kill anchor), ZERO PANE= reprints (no shell restart), tick counters monotonic across the gap (76→104→130→148→175→177 no reset), agent pid + all 4 child PIDs unchanged throughout. 4/4 panes consistent on all 4 cycles = the intermittency is gone. That SPAMMED a keychain password prompt ('Ghoztty[DEBUG] wants to use com.dzearing.ghoztty.relay-account') on EVERY launch — the user hit this live and stopped me. ROOT CAUSE: the debug bundle is AD-HOC signed (TeamIdentifier not set); the login-keychain ACL for the relay-account item is a trusted-application entry keyed by the app's exact cdhash (its designated requirement is `cdhash H"..."`). Re-signing mints a NEW cdhash not in the ACL -> prompt; a plain launch of the already-authorized zig-out cdhash (4d477ee3...) is silent (that's why T07 never prompted). Under ad-hoc signing there is NO way to change the binary silently — a real Sparkle upgrade is Developer-ID signed with a STABLE DR across versions, so it doesn't prompt; we can't replicate that. FIX: the swap keeps content byte-identical (same cdhash -> zero prompts), verified by comparing reserve vs installed cdhash before the run. This is immaterial to the AC: the restore path never reads app-bundle bytes (it reads the layout manifest + the surviving agent); the full FS-swap->relaunch->re-attach path IS exercised, and the app relaunches from a physically-replaced-on-disk bundle. The app ALWAYS launches from the installed zig-out path (never a /tmp copy) to guarantee the authorized cdhash. Teardown restores zig-out from the reserve if a crash ever interrupts a swap.

2026-07-15: done — MISDIAGNOSIS. There is NO app-side graceful-quit hang. The '~45s hang' was a TEST-HARNESS ZOMBIE-REAPING ARTIFACT, and the original T08 `sample` that pointed at _terminateFromSender/setupTabGroupObservation was a sample of the ALREADY-EXITED (zombie) process showing its frozen exit-path stack. Fix is harness-only (scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py); ZERO src/ or macos/ changes.

HOW I PROVED IT (per CLAUDE.md 'reproduce first'): reproduced the 45s via the harness (--quit=graceful reliably term=49.2s), then instrumented the app termination timeline with timestamped os_log/NSLog at applicationShouldTerminate, applicationWillTerminate (+before/after ipcServer.stop), windowWillClose, TerminalWindow.close, BaseTerminalController.deinit, ghostty_surface_free (Swift Task.detached), the Zig io_thread stop+join, AND a self-registered atexit handler. Timeline showed EVERYTHING completes in ~7ms: shouldTerminate→willTerminate→ipcServer.stop→all TerminalWindow.close→io_thread join DONE→atexit FIRED, all within milliseconds of the quit. The process then sat until the harness SIGKILLed it at 45s. `sample` couldn't attach (needs sudo; password-gated), so I inspected via a minimal Python repro that launches the app EXACTLY like the harness (subprocess.Popen, start_new_session, Popen handle discarded/unreaped) and, after an AppleScript quit, polled BOTH os.kill(pid,0) and `ps -o stat=`: within 0.6s ps_stat went Ss→Z (ZOMBIE) and STAYED Z for 30s+, while os.kill(pid,0) returned True the ENTIRE time; os.waitpid(pid,WNOHANG) then reaped it as (pid, 0) — conclusive. atexit fired in ms in that repro too.

ROOT CAUSE: the app exits cleanly and fast, but as a child of the Python harness it becomes a ZOMBIE (defunct) until reaped. The harness's pid_alive() used os.kill(pid,0), which reports a zombie as ALIVE until its parent waitpid()s it. graceful_quit() waits the full 45s for the pid to 'disappear', never reaps → times out → SIGKILL (no-op on a zombie) → 'hang'. (The kill -9 path never showed this because it caps wait_gone at a fixed 5s and ignores the result; graceful waited 45.) Neither pane count nor tab groups mattered — a zombie doesn't 'scale'; the earlier 'scales with pane/window count' was noise. The 'exec quits in 0.6s' comparison in T08 was measuring the true exit, not this harness's wait_gone.

FIX (scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py, harness-only): (1) pid_alive() rewritten to be zombie-aware — reap our own launched children first, then consult `ps -o state= -p PID` and treat a zombie (state starts 'Z') or a missing pid as NOT alive (a zombie has already run exit() → for 'has the app finished terminating?' it IS gone). (2) launch_app() now retains every Popen in a module list `_launched_procs`; new `_reap_children()` polls them (Popen.poll() reaps finished children) so a cleanly-exited app turns from zombie to truly-gone. (3) graceful_quit timeout 45→20s (now just a safety net; real exit is <1s) and corrected the misleading T08a comments in graceful_quit + the recovery-gap block.

(2) runListenUnix(): connect-probe stale-socket livecheck (probeUnixAlive: a successful connect ⇒ a live agent owns it ⇒ REFUSE with error.AlreadyListening rather than clobber; ECONNREFUSED/ENOENT ⇒ safe to unlink) → deleteFile stale node → makePath parent → std.net.Address.initUnix → bind under umask(0o177) so the node is created 0600 RACE-FREE (restore prev umask immediately after listen) → banner 'listening on unix:<path>' → same acceptLoop core as TCP with enforce_same_uid=true. (3) SECURITY GATE: acceptLoop gained an enforce_same_uid param; on the unix path it calls shouldServe(true, peerUid(fd), geteuid()) per accepted connection and CLOSEs + skips any peer that isn't us. peerUid() binds getpeereid(2) via an extern (cross-platform macOS LOCAL_PEERCRED / Linux SO_PEERCRED; not in Zig std) and returns null if the cred can't be read; shouldServe is a PURE decision (enforce off ⇒ always serve [TCP]; on ⇒ serve only a KNOWN uid == ours; unknown/null ⇒ REJECT — never serve a shell blind). The real LocalAgentManager path ~/.config/ghoztty/local-agent-debug/agent.sock fits. (b) did NOT fchmod the bound socket fd as belt-and-braces: on macOS fchmod of a socket returns EINVAL, which std.posix.fchmod maps to `unreachable` (PANIC) — the exact class of trap that once killed the agent via SO_NOSIGPIPE (socket_stream.zig). umask alone is sufficient AND safe (node born 0600, never briefly more permissive). std has no fchmodat either. tasks.title: Reboot floor (part 2): load-at-start materialization + RELAUNCH frame/handler
tasks.goal: On agent start, load sessions.json (T12) and materialize each record as a DEAD, relaunchable tombstone in the store (no child yet). New RELAUNCH protocol frame + agent handler: respawn the child under the recorded argv/cwd, re-key it into the same session id, transition the tombstone to alive, and stream fresh output. Additive/HELLO-compatible.
steps: session_meta.load() at agent start (runListen/runListenUnix) → for each record insert a tombstone Session (alive=false, no child, exit_code=null-or-a 'relaunchable' marker) carrying argv/cwd/title/pinned so ATTACH replies dead and LIST_SESSIONS shows it.
protocol.zig: RELAUNCH{session_id} + a reply (reuse OPENED/ATTACHED shape) — additive frame ids after the T10/T11 ones.
server.zig handleRelaunch: spawn a child from the recorded metadata, bind it to the existing id/channel, flip alive, reply. Persist (T12's persistMeta) after.
Decide the tombstone's exit_code semantics vs a real exited child (a relaunchable-on-load tombstone is distinct from a child that exited this run).

tasks.notes:
2026-07-16: done, impl commit 4f2fd3ec9. AGENT-SIDE + protocol + tests only (viewer relaunch UX = T12c; launchd = T12d). Additive/HELLO-compatible: two new frame ids + one new optional field on two existing replies; older peers ignore them.

TOMBSTONE SEMANTICS (the T12b design decision): added Session.relaunchable (session.zig) to distinguish a DISK-MATERIALIZED dead session (alive=false, relaunchable=true, exit_code=null, no child) from a child that GENUINELY EXITED this run (alive=false, relaunchable=false, exit_code set). This one bool drives everything: ATTACH replies dead+relaunchable so the viewer (T12c) knows to offer/auto-fire RELAUNCH vs. just an exited overlay; persistMeta KEEPS relaunchable tombstones (filter is now `!alive and !relaunchable` → skip) so a session loaded-but-not-yet-relaunched survives a SECOND restart (dropping it would silently lose the reboot-floor intent); RELAUNCH refuses a non-relaunchable tombstone (found-but-not-ok).

MATERIALIZATION (session.zig): SessionTable.materialize(rec, ring_bytes, now) re-keys the session to its RECORDED id (parseId of the 32-hex string — the viewer's layout manifest references THAT id, so it must NOT be re-minted), mints a fresh data channel, installs an inert deadChild() placeholder (new: a stateless no-op Child vtable — terminate/resize/signal no-op, tryWait null, write BrokenPipe — so table teardown is safe for a never-relaunched session and no allocation leaks), copies argv/cwd/title/pinned, PRESERVES created_ms but sets last_activity_ms=now (so a just-loaded session isn't instantly idle-reaped), allocates a full ring_bytes ring (used post-relaunch). Skips (returns null, no crash) a malformed or duplicate id → idempotent across a double load. SessionStore.loadPersisted(ring_bytes) reads meta_path via session_meta.load and materializes each record under the store lock; called ONCE at agent start in main.zig runListen/runListenUnix AFTER meta_path is set and BEFORE startReaper + accepting connections (verified live: the 'materialized N session(s)' log prints before the 'listening on' banner). No-op when --sessions-file absent or the file is missing (a clean box); a corrupt file logs + is swallowed (must not stop the agent booting).

RELAUNCH (server.zig handleRelaunch, protocol relaunch=0x26 / relaunched=0x27): mirrors handleOpen's lock discipline — validate + snapshot the relaunch inputs (argv/cwd dupes, channel) UNDER the store lock, DROP the lock, spawn the child OUTSIDE it (fork+exec must never run under the mutex that serializes every output chunk), then RE-LOCK + RE-FIND by id (the reaper could have evicted the tombstone during the spawn; if gone/re-keyed/already-alive, terminate the fresh child outside the lock and reply found=false/found=true-not-ok), install spawned.child over the deadChild placeholder, flip alive=true + relaunchable=false + exit_code=null, bindLocked to THIS connection, child.attach the reader to the store sink on the SAME channel, reply RELAUNCHED{ok,pid,found} on that channel, persistMeta. Reuses the session's EXISTING channel (the viewer already learned it from the dead ATTACHED frame) so output routes correctly and the reply frame's channel tells the client where the stream is. Synthesizes the OPEN as {command=recorded argv, cwd=recorded cwd, rows/cols from the RELAUNCH frame, pinned}. Two idempotent/edge branches before spawning: already-alive → rebind + reply ok (double RELAUNCH / race); not-found → reply on control channel, ok=false found=false (client falls back to a fresh OPEN).

FRESH-STREAM OFFSET (documented, client work in T12c): a materialized session has out_offset=0 + empty ring; the dead ATTACHED reply carried snapshot_at_offset=0; RELAUNCH streams fresh output from offset 0. The client must RESET its applied-offset baseline on RELAUNCHED (a relaunch is a FRESH stream, not a resync) or it would discard the first chunk (byte_offset 0 <= S 0). The RELAUNCHED reply is the signal; wiring the client reset + '--- restarted ---' banner is T12c.

TESTS (zig build test-agent exit 0, 481 total): protocol.zig — RELAUNCH/RELAUNCHED round-trip + relaunchable-tombstone SessionInfo round-trip (relaunchable survives, exit_code null). session.zig — materialize re-keys to the recorded id + dead/relaunchable/metadata/times + malformed/dup skip; loadPersisted materializes + persistMeta KEEPS the relaunchable tombstone but EXCLUDES a genuinely-exited one. server.zig — ATTACH to a materialized session is dead+relaunchable(no exit_code), RELAUNCH revives it (spawns via the fake spawner, session goes alive+!relaunchable, streams 'back!' at offset 0), and unknown-id RELAUNCH → ok=false found=false. Full app build OK (agent re-embedded).

LIVE VERIFIED (real ghoztty-agent binary, NOT the fake spawner): seeded a sessions.json with a pinned command record (argv='sleep 600', cwd=/tmp, title=sleeper, created_ms preserved) + a plain-shell record (null argv), ran the agent --listen-unix --sessions-file=<seed>, and `ghoztty +sessions --json` showed BOTH as alive:false pid:0 exit_code:null pinned:true with argv/cwd/title/created_at intact; agent stderr logged 'reboot floor: materialized 2 session(s) from disk' before the listening banner. loadPersisted is read-only (seed file unchanged). Box left clean (agent killed, port.json + tmp sockets removed). A full client-driven RELAUNCH against a real pty (viewer sends RELAUNCH, sees the process come back + banner) is exercised in T12c; the agent handler itself is proven by the fake-spawner server test.

KNOWN GAPS for T12c/T13 (not defects): (a) RELAUNCH treats the recorded argv as OPEN.command → the agent runs it via `<shell> -lic <argv>`. For a plain shell (argv null) this correctly spawns a fresh login shell; for a command session it re-runs the command. If a recorded argv is itself a full `<shell> -lic ...` wrapper (depends on what the client persisted at OPEN — T12 noted argv can be either the raw command or the shell path), it could double-wrap; the live viewer path (T12c) should confirm and, if needed, capture/relaunch the resolved argv verbatim (an OPEN.argv-style path already exists from T04c). (d) +sessions CLI doesn't yet surface the relaunchable flag in its table/JSON (the wire field is there; the CLI's OwnedSession parse just ignores it) — cosmetic, a one-line add if wanted.

APPROACH = in-terminal 'press any key to relaunch' handled ENTIRELY in the ZIG client backend (termio/Remote.zig + remote/connection.zig) — ZERO Swift/ABI, no overlay button, no protocol change. Chose this over the 'full' overlay-button path (steps' option a: new ABI flag + SwiftUI button + GUI->IO relaunch trigger) because it reuses the EXISTING relaunch machinery + the pane's own input path, is the lowest-risk change to the passing T12c/agent suites, and is terminal-native (mirrors Ghostty's own 'Press any key to close the terminal' idiom, inverted). The banner-only lightweight alternative was rejected: it is informational (no click wiring) and does NOT 'respawn in place' as acceptance requires.

KEY IDEA — SPLIT the relaunch into prepare + consent + send. Auto (T12c) does prepare-ring + send-RELAUNCH atomically in threadEnter. Prompt must NOT respawn the process until the user consents, so it brings up a LIVE-but-CHILDLESS pane (ring registered on the agent's known session channel, NO RELAUNCH sent) and defers the RELAUNCH to the first keystroke.

WIRING (2 files):
(1) src/remote/connection.zig — factored relaunchChannelCancellable into two reusable halves + refactored the auto path to call them (so all 3 original T12c tests still exercise the same code):
  * prepareRelaunchPane(session_id, channel) !*Pane — registers the inbound ring + creates a Pane with pid=0 (no child yet), discard_below=0/resync_active=false (fresh stream). This is the pre-RELAUNCH half; the ring pre-registration means the eventual respawn's first DATA (fresh prompt) is not dropped in the RELAUNCHED->register gap.
  * sendRelaunchOnPane(pane, rows, cols, px_w, px_h, canceller) !RelaunchResult{ok,found,pid} — sends RELAUNCH on the pane's channel, awaits RELAUNCHED, fills pane.pid on ok. On !ok leaves the pane INTACT (childless) — unlike the auto RelaunchOutcome path which tears it down — so the prompt surface can show a 'relaunch failed' note and threadExit detaches it cleanly.
  * relaunchChannelCancellable = prepareRelaunchPane + errdefer teardownPane + sendRelaunchOnPane; on !ok explicitly teardownPane + return pane=null (a value-return doesn't fire errdefer, so no double-free). Behavior byte-identical to before for the auto path.
(2) src/termio/Remote.zig — new `awaiting_relaunch: bool` on the STABLE Remote backend (touched only on the IO thread: threadEnter->queueWrite, so no sync needed). threadEnter: added a `.dead and relaunchable and policy==.prompt` branch AFTER the auto branch that calls prepareRelaunchPane(sid, outcome.channel), sets awaiting_relaunch=true, and `break :pane p` (brings the pane up normally — full ThreadData/ring_async/drain machinery unchanged, since a real *Pane exists). After bring-up the divider block gained an `else if (self.awaiting_relaunch)` that injects the prompt `\r\n[1m[ Session ended ][0m [2m— press any key to relaunch[0m\r\n` via processOutput (mirrors the auto '--- session restarted ---' divider injection). queueWrite: added an early branch — if awaiting_relaunch and data.len>0, call performAwaitedRelaunch(td) and swallow the byte(s) (no child yet); an empty write (focus report) is ignored so it can't spuriously fire. performAwaitedRelaunch (new): clears the flag FIRST (a racing second keystroke can't double-fire), calls sendRelaunchOnPane with the CURRENT grid/screen size + &self.canceller (so teardown's shutdown()->canceller.cancel() wakes a parked RELAUNCH — same park-on-IO-thread pattern as threadEnter's auto relaunch), on ok injects '--- session restarted ---' + drainRing(td) for immediacy; on err/!ok injects a '--- relaunch failed ---' note and leaves the pane (detaches on threadExit).

WHY the pane-exists design (vs a pane-less awaiting state): keeping a real *Pane (via prepareRelaunchPane) means resize/threadExit/drainRing/ring_async all work UNCHANGED — no ThreadData.pane optionality, no new backend union arm, no restructure of the drain path. The only new state is one bool + one queueWrite branch.

UX note: the affordance is keypress-driven (any key that produces input relaunches; the pane must be focused). A raw mouse click only focuses (mouse reporting is off on a dead pane, so it produces no queueWrite input) — 'press any key' is the honest, discoverable trigger and matches acceptance's 'on click/keypress'.

2026-07-16: done, commit 03a781207. SWIFT (LocalAgentManager.swift) + Python E2E + docs only; ZERO Zig/protocol/agent changes (the RELAUNCH machinery from T12b/T12c is what recovers — this task just makes launchd OWN the agent so it comes back after a kill/reboot, then proves it E2E).

DESIGN DECISION (bootstrap vs find-or-spawn): made launchd the SOLE spawner on the normal path, NOT a second racing spawner beside posix_spawn. Reason: the agent single-instance guard makes a LOSER exit 183 (nonzero); if a KeepAlive launchd job were the loser it would tight-respawn-loop (launchd restarts nonzero exits). So connect() now: dialExisting -> else ensureLaunchAgentLoaded() (write plist + `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID` + kickstart) + pollDial; posix_spawn spawnAndDial kept ONLY as a fallback when launchctl is unavailable (no Aqua/gui session) — that path has no KeepAlive so no loop. One owner per path = no guard race. Matches design §5.2 ('the app writes the plist on first use ... also spawns on-demand ... single-instance guard handles the race').

LocalAgentManager wiring: Paths gains `home` + `launchAgentLabel` (debug=com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug.agent, release=com.dzearing.ghoztty.agent — DISTINCT so KeepAlive jobs never collide) + launchAgentPlistURL (~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist, always under the REAL home — gui/<uid> only reads there). ensureLaunchAgentLoaded: creates the 0700 agent dir (launchd won't), writes the plist via PropertyListSerialization (auto-escapes paths) ONLY when changed, bootout+bootstrap on change else kickstart, treats bootstrap rc=5 ('already bootstrapped') as benign. Plist: ProgramArguments = agent + --listen-unix/--port-file/--sessions-file (same as spawnDetached); EnvironmentVariables = GHOSTTY_AGENT_LOCK/HEARTBEAT/NO_SELFUPDATE (launchd does NOT inherit app env) + SHELL/PATH/LANG copied from the app so the agent resolves the same login shell; RunAtLoad+KeepAlive+ProcessType=Interactive+StandardOut/ErrPath=agent.log+WorkingDirectory=home. pollDial() extracted + shared by both paths. uninstallLaunchAgent() exposed for teardown. 3 new Swift tests (distinct labels, plist-under-real-home, sessions.json sibling); targeted xcodebuild test of both LocalAgentManager suites PASS.

E2E (scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py --agent-restart): reboot-equivalent (NOT agent-only-crash — see gap below). Per cycle: SIGKILL app+agent, assert launchd KeepAlive restarts the agent (NEW pid, ≤5s), relaunch app -> manifest restore -> re-attach -> auto-RELAUNCH. assert_reboot_cycle asserts the OPPOSITE of survival: agent pid CHANGED, every pane child pid NEW, `--- session restarted ---` banner present, marker re-ran, topology still exact from the manifest. full_reset now launchctl-bootouts the debug job + removes the plist FIRST (KeepAlive would instantly undo a bare agent SIGKILL, and it must not linger). LAUNCHD THROTTLE TRAP (hit+fixed): KeepAlive respawns are rate-limited to once per ThrottleInterval (10s) since last spawn — rapid cycles 2/3 saw 'no restart in 8s'. Fix = settle each live agent past a 12s floor before killing (measures the real single-crash latency, not a throttle artifact). SECOND TRAP: `ps -o etimes=` is NOT a valid keyword on this macOS ps (dumps the keyword list) — so track the agent spawn wall-clock in Python instead of querying ps.

Box left CLEAN after every run (job booted out, plist removed, no lingering agent). Design doc acceptance table + scripts/e2e/README.md updated with the AC3/AC4 row + throttle/cleanliness notes.

GAP -> T12e: in-place AC4 (agent crashes while the app STAYS UP) does NOT auto-recover today — the Zig client backend does not auto-redial a dropped local link (connection.zig controlReaderLoop returns on EOF, LinkState FSM only computes backoff; its own header says it 'does NOT actually reconnect'), and the local machine pill + Reconnect button are hidden for isLocalMachine. So an agent-only crash leaves panes dead until an app relaunch. --agent-restart therefore drives the reboot-equivalent (kill app+agent, relaunch app) which is exactly what the acceptance sanctions ('reboot-equivalent simulated by full agent restart'). True in-place reconnect+relaunch is split to T12e.

tasks.title: Reboot scrollback: ring disk snapshots
tasks.goal: Agent snapshots dirty rings every 30s + on SIGTERM; after restart, replay snapshot then a divider then live output (design §5.4).
steps: Snapshot format (offset+bytes), atomic write, load on start attaching to relaunched session; tests.

tasks.notes:
2026-07-16: done, feature commit 1568e76c9. SCOPE: SIGTERM-on-graceful-agent-shutdown split out to new T13b (needs safe signal handling; NOT exercised by the E2E which SIGKILLs, and the connection-drop trigger already covers real logout/reboot). Everything else shipped.

NEW FILE src/remote/agent/ring_snapshot.zig — compact BINARY format `<rings_dir>/<id>.ring`: magic 'GRS1' + base_offset(u64 LE) + byte_len(u64 LE) + bytes. Atomic tmp+fsync+rename (mirrors session_meta.writeAtomic but two writeAlls to avoid concatenating the 2MB ring). load() is best-effort: absent/short-header/wrong-magic/length-mismatch ALL -> null (a corrupt snapshot must never stop a session relaunching; the pane just comes back blank). delete() for CLOSE/reap cleanup. std-only, standalone tests. Added to agent_test.zig.

ARCHITECTURE (key decisions):
(1) TRIGGERS: NOT the SIGKILL'd agent's own death (impossible) but (a) periodic every 30 reaper ticks and (b) on VIEWER DISCONNECT [server.zig shutdown -> detachAll -> store.snapshotRings]. (b) is what makes the reboot E2E pass without a 30s wait: the E2E SIGKILLs the APP first, the still-alive agent sees the dropped socket -> snapshots -> THEN the agent is SIGKILLed. This app-first-kill ordering is also what a real logout does. In-place mode (--agent-only) kills ONLY the agent so NO snapshot fires -> pre-restart scrollback legitimately lost there (honest contract); the E2E asserts scrollback ONLY for reboot, not in-place.
(2) REPLAY: materialized dead session's ring is PRELOADED at start (loadPersisted->preloadRingSnapshot): renumbered to base 0 = [snapshot][divider], out_offset at tail. On RELAUNCH (handleRelaunch phase 3, under lock before child.attach) the agent copies that ring and sendData's it to the viewer BEFORE the fresh child's live output -> client sees scrollback->divider->live with NO offset hole (relaunch pane keeps every byte from 0).
(3) DIVIDER OWNERSHIP: baked into the RING (between snapshot and live), NOT client-side — the client's synchronous processOutput(divider) can't be sequenced between async ring drains, so a client-side divider would land BEFORE the replayed scrollback (wrong order) AND double up. So agent bakes+replays; adds protocol.Relaunched.replayed (additive, threaded through RelaunchResult/RelaunchOutcome); client (termio/Remote.zig) suppresses its OWN divider when replayed=true, keeps it for the no-snapshot case. Same divider STRING as the client's so RESTART_DIVIDER still matches.
(4) MEMORY BOUND: snapshotRings copies ONE ring at a time (collect dirty ids under lock; per-id re-lock/copy-to-reused-buffer/unlock/write) — never all 256x2MB at once, never OS I/O under the store lock. Dirty bit = out_offset != last_snapshot_offset; marked clean only after a successful write.

E2E CHANGES (tricky): with T13 a reboot pane's scrollback is [OLD marker+ticks][divider][FRESH marker+ticks] — TWO PANE= lines. parse_marker returns the FIRST (old) -> broke 'fresh pid != baseline' AND wait_restored returned as soon as the REPLAYED old marker appeared (before fresh output -> pane-3 flake on first run). FIXES: fresh_marker(text) = marker AFTER the last divider (fallback to first when no divider); assert_reboot_cycle uses it for fresh pid + asserts 'PANE=n ' appears BEFORE the divider (pre-restart proof); wait_restored(relaunched=True) + wait_inplace_recovered require a POST-divider marker.

tasks.title: Reboot scrollback part 2: snapshot dirty rings on graceful agent SIGTERM

steps: SAFE signal handling only: do NOT do work in an async signal handler (locks/malloc/file I/O unsafe there, and snapshotRings takes the store mutex). Use sigwait: block SIGTERM process-wide on the main thread BEFORE spawning accept/reaper/writer threads (they inherit the mask), then a dedicated watcher thread calls std.c.sigwait; on receipt run store.snapshotRings() then std.process.exit(0). Verify std.c.sigwait links on this macOS build before committing.

Gate to POSIX (Windows has the tray Exit path). Must NOT regress T12d/T12e launchd flows (KeepAlive+RunAtLoad): a clean exit(0) on SIGTERM is correct; confirm the watcher actually exits so launchd's SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation isn't needed.
Test: SIGTERM (not SIGKILL) a live agent with a dirty session and assert the ring file was written before exit.

APPROACH = block SIGTERM process-wide + a dedicated sigwait WATCHER thread (NO async signal handler — snapshotRings takes the store mutex + does file I/O, both unsafe from a handler interrupting an arbitrary thread). All in src/remote/agent/main.zig. WIRING (3 pieces): (1) blockSigterm() — pthread_sigmask(SIG.BLOCK, {SIGTERM}) on the MAIN thread, called at the top of BOTH the .listen and .listen_unix arms in main() BEFORE acquireDaemonLockOrExit. This ordering is LOAD-BEARING: acquireDaemonLockOrExit spawns the single-instance HEARTBEAT thread, so the block must precede it — every subsequently-spawned thread (heartbeat, reaper, ring watcher, per-conn workers) inherits the block, so a process-directed SIGTERM lands on no default handler and stays pending for the watcher's sigwait. (2) startSigtermWatcher(&store) — spawns a detached watcher, called in runListen + runListenUnix right after loadPersisted, before startReaper (store exists by then). (3) sigtermWatcherLoop — while(std.c.sigwait(&set,&signo)!=0){} then store.snapshotRings() then std.process.exit(0). The clean exit(0) means launchd's SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation is never needed (T12d/T12e KeepAlive flows still restart it). POSIX-only via `if (builtin.os.tag == .windows) return;` in blockSigterm+startSigtermWatcher (Windows graceful stop is the tray Exit path).
